variants.description: Dermatomyositis: an immune-mediated disease of skin and muscle in Shetland Sheepdogs and Collies, causing hair loss and scabs on the face, ears and legs, sometimes with muscle wasting. Risk comes from a combination of the PAN2 and MAP3K7CL variants and a DLA immune-type haplotype; one marker alone means only modestly raised risk.

variants.description: A heart-muscle disease in which the wall of the left ventricle thickens abnormally; in the Golden Retriever family where it was found, affected puppies died suddenly before two years of age. Recessive.

variants.description: A connective-tissue disorder with fragile, overly stretchy skin that tears easily; found in Chihuahuas and Poodles. Recessive.
A combination of poorly formed, easily worn tooth enamel and slowed nerve conduction (a mild peripheral neuropathy), described in Lancashire Heelers. Recessive.
A form of progressive retinal atrophy, in which the light-sensing cells of the retina degenerate and vision is gradually lost; found in a Labrador Retriever family. Recessive.
Thyroglobulin deficiency: the thyroid cannot make normal hormone, causing dwarfism, limb deformities, thick skin and slow development in puppies. Described in Rottweilers. Recessive.
The split (double) nose that is a hallmark of the Turkish Çatalburun breed; a physical trait, not a disease.
A disorder of the brain's nerve insulation (myelin) causing head and body tremors from birth; described in Toy Poodles. Recessive.

variants.trait: Progressive retinal atrophy, Miniature Schnauzer, type 1
variants.phene_name: Progressive retinal atrophy, Miniature Schnauzer, type 1
variants.description: A form of progressive retinal atrophy in Miniature Schnauzers: the retina gradually degenerates, with night blindness first and later loss of day vision. Recessive.
A slowly progressive degeneration of nerve fibres causing hind-limb weakness and an unsteady gait in young adult dogs; described in Miniature American Shepherds. Recessive.
An inherited metabolic brain disease causing early-onset movement disorders (unsteady gait, abnormal limb movements) in young Eurasier dogs. Recessive.

Degeneration of the cerebellum (the brain's coordination centre) causing a progressive wobbly gait and head tremors in puppies. Reported in a single mixed-breed dog with one copy of a new (de novo) variant.
A lysosomal storage disease: a missing sugar-processing enzyme lets waste build up in cells, causing progressive neurological decline in young dogs. Reported in a Doberman Pinscher. Recessive.
A mitochondrial energy disorder of the brain causing progressive unsteadiness and abnormal muscle tone in puppies; found in a Jack Russell Terrier x Chihuahua litter. Recessive.
A congenital disorder of the insulation around peripheral nerves, causing weakness from a young age; described in Golden Retrievers. Recessive.
Abnormal glycogen (sugar store) builds up in heart and other muscles; described in young adult Basset Hounds. Recessive.
Thickened, hard paw pads on all feet. Reported in a single Labrador Retriever with one copy of a new (de novo) variant.
Low activity of a liver detoxifying enzyme (GSTT5). Not a disease, but dogs with two copies may process some drugs and chemicals differently; common in Beagles and Pembroke Welsh Corgis. Recessive.
An inherited heart-muscle disease in which puppies can die suddenly; found in Manchester Terriers. Recessive with complete penetrance: dogs with two copies are affected.

variants.trait: Addison's disease and multiple autoimmune syndrome
variants.phene_name: Addison's disease and multiple autoimmune syndrome
variants.description: Juvenile-onset Addison's disease (adrenal gland failure), often with other autoimmune problems, in Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers. Recessive; about three in four dogs with two copies develop early-onset disease.
A slowly progressive brain disease of Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers, with violent movements during sleep, anxiety, noise sensitivity and later cognitive and gait problems. Recessive.
A muscle disease caused by a lack of creatine, with muscle wasting, exercise intolerance and an enlarged oesophagus; in the reported family, signs improved with creatine supplements. Recessive.

variants.variant_breed: Beagle Huntaway New Zealand Heading Dog
variants.description: Dogs with two copies lack a working CYP1A2 liver enzyme and clear certain drugs slowly. Not a disease, but worth sharing with your vet; first found in Beagles. Recessive.

Persistently high blood calcium with low calcium in the urine, caused by a faulty calcium-sensing receptor; reported in a Border Collie cross. Knowing about it can spare a dog unnecessary parathyroid surgery. Recessive.
A rare bleeding disorder in which blood clots are unstable, causing spontaneous or prolonged bleeding; reported in a Black and Tan Coonhound. Recessive.
Generalised scaly, thickened skin with paw pad, hair and tooth abnormalities. Reported in a single Miniature Poodle with one copy of a new (de novo) variant.
Very pale coat, skin and eyes with light sensitivity ('white Doberman' and similar), caused by a pigment transporter defect. Recessive.

variants.variant_breed: Lhasa Apso Mixed Breed Pekingese Pomeranian
variants.description: Very pale coat, skin and eyes with light sensitivity ('white Doberman' and similar), caused by a pigment transporter defect. Recessive.
An inherited skin disorder with generalised scaling from puppyhood; reported in a Chihuahua. Recessive.
A disorder of the nerve-muscle junction behind 'dancing Doberman' and 'duck walking' gaits: hind-limb weakness, muscle wasting and fatigue in Doberman Pinschers. Recessive.
An inherited immune deficiency causing pneumonia (including Pneumocystis), gut and skin disease; found in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels. Recessive.
Retinal degeneration together with tremors and episodes resembling seizures; described in Cirneco dell'Etna dogs. Recessive.
Episodes of muscle stiffness and abnormal movement triggered by exercise or stress, in Shetland Sheepdogs. Dominant: one copy can cause it.
A disorder of cell-membrane fat production causing progressive retinal, brain and nerve degeneration; described in Saarloos Wolfdogs. Recessive.
A risk marker for pituitary-dependent hyperadrenocorticism (Cushing's disease: excess cortisol causing thirst, appetite and coat changes), found in Poodles. Raises risk; not a diagnosis.
A slowly progressive neurological disease of adult Weimaraners, with incoordination, weakness and cognitive decline.
An immune deficiency that leaves dogs vulnerable to systemic infection with Mycobacterium avium, a germ that rarely harms other dogs; found in Miniature Schnauzers. Recessive.
A slowly progressive stiff, high-stepping gait in an adult Jack Russell Terrier. Recessive.
Patches of thick, tree-bark-like skin. X-linked: one copy can cause it in females (often in streaks along the body) and males with the variant are affected.

An X-linked form of progressive retinal atrophy in English Cocker Spaniels: affected males lose vision from about 3-4 years of age; females with one copy are carriers.
Malformed drainage angle of the eye (pectinate ligament dysplasia) that can lead to painful, sight-threatening glaucoma; found in Border Collies. Recessive.
A progressive degeneration of the brain, spinal cord and nerves causing incoordination and stiffness from a few months of age; described in Great Pyrenees. Recessive.

variants.variant_breed: Chinese Crested Peruvian Hairless Dog Xoloitzcuintli
variants.description: The variant that makes Chinese Crested, Peruvian Hairless and Xoloitzcuintli dogs hairless, often with missing teeth. One copy gives the hairless type; two copies are thought to be lethal before birth, so hairless dogs carry one copy.

A severe neurological disease of puppies (weakness, cramping and falling) found in the Markiesje (Dutch Tulip Hound). Different from degenerative myelopathy, which involves another SOD1 variant. Recessive.
Growth retardation, hair loss, unerupted teeth and eye abnormalities, including glaucoma; described in Segugio Italiano dogs. Recessive.
Progressive incoordination with retinal degeneration and severe anemia; reported in a single mixed-breed dog. Recessive.
Puppies born without front legs; described in Chihuahuas. Recessive. The screen reads the three linked variants reported for it.

Overactive parathyroid glands raising blood calcium, usually in older Keeshonden (over 8 years); treatable once found. Dominant with high age-related penetrance: one copy raises the risk.
Hair loss on the thighs of sighthounds such as Greyhounds and Whippets. The variant is a risk factor found in nearly all Greyhounds; cosmetic, not painful.

A kidney disease in which protein leaks into the urine, mostly in adult Soft-Coated Wheaten Terriers. This variant is one of two linked risk markers (with NPHS1); risk is highest with two copies of both.
Life-long green urine caused by a missing bile-pigment enzyme; reported in mixed-breed dogs. Usually harmless on its own. Recessive.

Small eyes from birth together with stunted growth, enamel defects, anemia and low platelets; found in Portuguese Water Dogs. Recessive.
Puppies move their legs in synchrony (a hopping, 'bunny hop' gait) instead of alternating; described in Weimaraners. Recessive.
Defective removal of immune cells, causing enlarged lymph nodes and spleen and low blood-cell counts in young Boerboels. Recessive.
A connective-tissue disorder (fibrillin) affecting the heart, joints and lungs; reported in a single Golden Retriever puppy carrying one copy of a deletion.

variants.description: A severe skin-fragility disease: the skin and mouth lining blister and erode at the slightest friction. Recessive.

variants.variant_breed: Basset Bleu de Gascogne Small Swiss Hound
variants.description: A fatal lysosomal storage disease causing progressive loss of vision, coordination and cognition, starting around one year of age. Recessive.
A scaly-skin disorder: dogs develop flaky, dark scales, usually mild and lifelong. Common in Golden Retrievers; another variant in the same gene occurs in Labradors. Recessive.
A candidate cause of splitting of the retinal layers that can impair vision, found in a Pomeranian. X-linked: affected males; females with one copy are carriers.

variants.variant_breed: English Springer Spaniel Welsh Springer Spaniel
variants.description: Blood clots dissolve too quickly, causing spontaneous or post-surgical bleeding; found in English and Welsh Springer Spaniels. Tell your vet before any surgery. Recessive.
The tiny hairs (cilia) that clear the airways do not beat properly, causing chronic cough, nasal discharge and pneumonia from puppyhood; found in Cocker Spaniels. Recessive.
Low vitamin E causes retinal degeneration and sometimes unsteadiness in English Cocker Spaniels; early vitamin E supplementation may help. Recessive.
A disorder of copper transport; reported in a Cavalier King Charles Spaniel with kidney (Fanconi) problems, poor growth and incoordination. X-linked: males with one copy are affected.
Early loss of day vision (cone-rod dystrophy) in Standard Poodles. Recessive.
